name: bluebird-promisify-multiargs-talk-node-sdk
behavioral_change: In bluebird v_new (3.0.0), `Promise.promisify` and `Promise.promisifyAll` by default resolve the promise with only the first success value passed to the node-style callback, whereas v_old (2.x) collected multiple success values into an array. The call form is unchanged and no exception is raised by the library itself; the old array behaviour is restored with the new `multiArgs: true` option.
downstream_effect: talk-node-sdk's src/client.coffee promisifies the `request` module and consumes results with `.spread (res, body) ->`; after the upgrade the promise resolves to the bare response object, `.spread` throws inside the promise chain, and seven mocha tests time out with `done()` never called. The timeout lines carry no stack frames; the only frames come from unhandled rejections pointing at test/main.coffee, src/worker.coffee and bluebird internals, none of which is the file to edit (src/client.coffee), and promisify or spread never appear.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in src/client.coffee, adding `multiArgs: true` to the `Promise.promisify` call on line 3.
documented_in: bluebird's "New in bluebird 3.0" document (docs/docs/new-in-bluebird-3.md, tag v3.7.2), section Promisification API changes, states in prose that promisification now uses only the first callback argument and that a new boolean option `multiArgs` restores the array behaviour. The document gives only prose for this change and no code showing `Promise.promisify(fn, {multiArgs: true})`.
failing_tests: Talk#Main retry connecting should work when api server is started after the client
Talk#Main client and call apis should get an NO_PERMISSIONT error without authorization
Talk#Main client and call apis should call the user.readOne with authorization
Talk#Main worker and test for what he should do should run the tasks every 100ms
